name: Maldives
snapshot: An Indian Ocean archipelago of luxury resorts and rising seas, led by Mohamed Muizzu, who has balanced between India and China while grappling with heavy debt.
culture: The Maldives' 1,200 coral islands are spread over 26 atolls. Dhivehi, written in its own Thaana script, is the national language. Bodu beru drumming accompanies dance and song. Islam is central, and citizenship is reserved for Muslims.
society: Tourism to private island resorts provides most income. Most land is less than a metre above sea level, making the country one of the most exposed to climate change. Debt, much of it to China and India, has raised default fears. A youthful population faces limited jobs outside tourism.
situation: Mohamed Muizzu won in 2023 on an "India Out" campaign and asked Indian military personnel to leave, then mended ties with New Delhi in 2024 amid a debt squeeze. His party won a supermajority in 2024 parliamentary elections, and media and judicial independence have come under pressure.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years, at most two terms, and heads the government; parliament, the People's Majlis, is dominated by Muizzu's party.
